summary: Backend testing of GET /api/admin/purge-test-devices browser variant + POST regression. 19/20 tests pass. One real security bug found: preview page does NOT HTML-escape user_id → stored-XSS since /api/register-push is unauthenticated and any client can plant a payload that fires when an admin opens the preview URL. Auth (no/wrong token → 401 HTML 'Wrong password'), preview-without-delete, confirm=yes delete (Deleted: 4, Remaining: 1), idempotent re-confirm (Deleted: 0), empty-preview 'Nothing matching to delete.', POST header auth, POST no-header 401 JSON, trigger-alert regression, register-push upsert, legacy /api/status, all 6 removed debug endpoints returning 404, and shared _run_purge_test_devices helper usage — all verified. Note: register-push returns 500 in this env because EMERGENT_PUSH_KEY=placeholder, but DB upsert has already succeeded before the relay call, so purge tests still pass (test file tolerates 201-or-500 for /api/register-push). No lint errors in server.py.

critical.issue:
Stored-XSS: preview page renders each matched row via f-string `
  • {m.get('user_id')}...` (server.py:239) with no html.escape(). Any client can POST to the UNAUTHENTICATED /api/register-push with a user_id like `TEST_` and that payload will execute in the admin's Safari when they open the preview URL. Same risk applies to platform value (also f-stringed unescaped). Fix: `import html` and wrap `html.escape(m.get('user_id') or '')` and `html.escape(m.get('platform') or '?')`.

minor.issue: Returns HTTP 500 in this environment because EMERGENT_PUSH_KEY=placeholder — the relay returns 401 which is translated to 500 (server.py:96). The DB row IS upserted BEFORE the relay call, so functionally the row is registered. Consider swallowing relay-auth failures the same way (log + return 201) rather than exposing an internal 500 to callers whose row was actually saved. Not blocking, but a caller cannot distinguish 'never saved' from 'saved but relay unavailable'.

action_items: SECURITY (HIGH): HTML-escape user_id and platform in server.py:239 and anywhere else the preview/result templates interpolate DB values. Use `import html` + `html.escape(...)` (or Jinja2 autoescape).

Confirm the accompanying `<a href="?token=Pt3481pt&confirm=yes">` embeds the token directly in a link — that is fine for the intended Safari-copy-paste UX, but be aware Referer headers on any external click from the preview page will leak the admin token; consider `<meta name="referrer" content="no-referrer">` on both HTML pages.

Optional: make POST /api/register-push return 201 even if the Emergent relay is unavailable, since the local DB write succeeds first — currently the placeholder key makes register-push always look like 500 to callers.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py:239 — f-string interpolation of MongoDB values into HTML without escaping is an XSS sink. Same file uses no template engine, so all HTML must be manually escaped.

server.py:80-104 — DB upsert precedes relay call; a relay 401 aborts the response with 500 but leaves the row in the DB. Consider swapping order (relay first) or logging-only for relay failures for consistency.
seed_data_creation: Test file wipes push_devices collection (direct mongo) then seeds TEST_a1, test-b1, diag-c1, dashboard, qg-legit-1 via /api/register-push. Cleaned up at end of TestConfirmDelete + TestRegression.test_register_push_upserts.
context_for_next_testing_agent: After main agent adds html.escape to server.py:239, rerun `pytest /app/backend/tests/test_purge_browser.py -v`. TestHtmlEscaping::test_script_tag_in_user_id_not_executed should flip green. All other tests should stay green. The test file uses direct pymongo to wipe push_devices before seeding — if MONGO_URL changes, update env vars. Backend URL used: http://localhost:8001.
rca_of_issue:
XSS RCA: server.py line 238-241 builds `
  • {m.get('user_id')} ({m.get('platform') or '?'})
    • ` inside an f-string. Neither value is passed through html.escape. `/api/register-push` (server.py:76) accepts any user_id string with no auth and upserts it into db.push_devices. The purge preview endpoint later reads and interpolates those raw strings back into the returned HTML. Reproduction: (1) POST /api/register-push {user_id: 'TEST_', platform:'android', device_token:'x'}; (2) GET /api/admin/purge-test-devices?token=Pt3481pt in Safari; (3) alert fires. Mitigation: escape both values (and also escape `token` if you ever choose to reflect it, though currently only used inside href which is safer). One-line fix: `import html` at top, replace `{m.get('user_id')}` with `{html.escape(str(m.get('user_id') or ''))}` and `{m.get('platform') or '?'}` with `{html.escape(str(m.get('platform') or '?'))}`.
